scope: M5 first increment: six fixture scenarios, twelve questions and extra approved S04 follow-up. No business execution.

semantic_review.reviewer: Codex, reviewed all thirteen actual answers and registered fixture sources
passed: All twelve main questions had the independently required observed category and minimum source evidence.
S01/S02/S03 follow-ups did not claim actual input/SQL/data modifications or offer retry actions.
S03 retained both input-batch and existing-target duplicate possibilities, without excluding other deeper causes.
S04 used the two-button approval path, did not treat chat as approval, retained simulation boundaries and did not propose another retry after child creation.
S05 remained UNKNOWN/NEEDS_CONFIRMATION, with no extra-detail acquisition or reclassification-based retry offer.

wording_risks.issue: missing_information questioned whether the error was real-upstream or fixture even though task_data_source is explicitly FIXTURE. Source uncertainty is unnecessary and potentially confusing; UI source labels and actual tool data remain FIXTURE.
next_steps mentioned UNKNOWN/DUPLICATE together even though the finding correctly remained DUPLICATE_DATA. No button existed, but advice also unnecessarily referred to retry buttons.
Responses expose internal policy/property names and repeat checklist items. These are usability issues, not completed production language quality.

semantic_review.limits: Fixed questions were reused for development and repair. No holdout accuracy, first-call stability, real network-failure, cross-browser or production quality claim. This does not mark the entire M5 accepted.
